title: Indian Flora, Fauna, Institutions, Acts & Policies

questions.q:
Match the endemic animal with the region to which it is restricted in India:
A. Nilgiri tahr
B. Hangul
C. Sangai
D. Namdapha flying squirrel
1. Western Ghats
2. Dachigam, Kashmir valley
3. Loktak Lake region, Manipur
4. Arunachal Pradesh
questions.e: The tahr lives on the grassy hills of the Western Ghats, the Hangul in Dachigam, the Sangai in Keibul Lamjao on Loktak and the flying squirrel only in Namdapha.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q: The Silent Valley movement of the 1970s in Kerala was launched to oppose a hydroelectric project because the project would have:
o: displaced the Great Indian Bustard from grasslands
flooded rainforest that is a habitat of the lion-tailed macaque
questions.e: The proposed dam on the Kunthipuzha river threatened one of the last undisturbed tropical rainforests of the Western Ghats. The campaign led to the creation of Silent Valley National Park in 1984.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna
questions.h: Silent Valley: saved macaque, dam dropped

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about cheetahs in India:
1. The Asiatic cheetah was officially declared extinct in India in 1952.
2. In 2022, cheetahs from Namibia were introduced into Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh.
3. Kuno National Park is located in Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Hunting and habitat loss wiped out the cheetah in India, and the government declared it extinct in 1952. Kuno lies in Madhya Pradesh, and the reintroduction programme is called Project Cheetah.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Gangetic river dolphin:
1. It was declared the National Aquatic Animal of India.
2. The Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary is in Bihar.
3. It is found only in the Brahmaputra river.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The species is found in the Ganga, Brahmaputra and Meghna river systems, not only the Brahmaputra. It is a blind, echolocating mammal and an indicator of river health.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q: In India, the Indus river dolphin is found in which of the following rivers?
questions.e: The Indus dolphin is a subspecies of the South Asian river dolphin, mostly in Pakistan's Indus system, with a small population in the Beas river in India.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the olive ridley turtle:
1. It is known for mass nesting (arribada) on the Odisha coast.
2. Rushikulya is one of its mass nesting sites.
3. Gahirmatha Marine Sanctuary lies in Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Gahirmatha is off the Odisha coast near Bhitarkanika, so statement 3 is incorrect. Mass nesting happens in winter and early spring.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q: The major cause of the catastrophic decline of Indian vultures in the 1990s and 2000s was:
o: loss of nesting trees to coastal erosion
the veterinary drug diclofenac, which poisoned vultures feeding on treated cattle carcasses
questions.e: Diclofenac causes kidney failure in vultures. India banned its veterinary use in 2006, and a breeding centre was set up at Pinjore, Haryana.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q:
Match the species with the protected area known for it:
A. Great Indian Bustard
B. Pygmy hog
C. Hoolock gibbon
D. Hard-ground barasingha
1. Manas National Park
2. Kanha National Park
3. Desert National Park
4. Hollongapar Gibbon Wildlife Sanctuary
questions.e: The bustard is a Thar bird, the pygmy hog is linked to Manas, Hollongapar in Assam protects hoolock gibbons, and Kanha saved the hard-ground barasingha.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q: Neelakurinji (Strobilanthes kunthiana), which blooms en masse once in about twelve years, is associated with the:
o: shola grasslands of the Western Ghats
questions.e: Its mass blooming turns the hills of the Nilgiris and Munnar in the Western Ghats blue-violet. Kurinji is the Sangam Tamil name for hill landscapes.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q:
Statement-I: Nepenthes khasiana, the pitcher plant endemic to Meghalaya, traps insects.
Statement-II: It grows in nitrogen-poor soils and gets nitrogen from digested insects.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Pitcher plants in nutrient-poor, acidic soils supplement nitrogen by trapping and digesting insects. Statement-II explains the carnivorous habit in Statement-I.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Flora

questions.q: Red sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus), whose smuggling is a recurring concern, is endemic to:
o: the Eastern Ghats region of southern Andhra Pradesh
questions.e: The tree grows naturally in the Seshachalam and Palakonda hills. Its wood is prized abroad for its colour, creating a smuggling incentive.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Flora

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Project Tiger:
1. It was launched in 1973 from Jim Corbett National Park.
2. The tiger reserve system has core and buffer areas, with the core kept free of human disturbance.
3. Sariska was among the nine tiger reserves with which the project began.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The original nine were Corbett, Bandipur, Kanha, Manas, Melghat, Palamau, Ranthambore, Similipal and Sundarbans. Sariska was added later.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q: Which of the following was NOT among the nine tiger reserves originally established under Project Tiger in 1973?
questions.e: Periyar in Kerala was added later in 1978. The original set also included Corbett, Bandipur, Melghat, Palamau, Similipal and Sundarbans.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA):
1. It became a statutory body through an amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
2. The Union Minister in charge of environment chairs it.
3. It is headquartered at Dehradun.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The NTCA was given statutory status in 2006 after Sariska lost its tigers to poaching. It is headquartered in New Delhi; the Wildlife Institute of India is in Dehradun.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q: The goal of doubling wild tiger numbers by 2022, known as Tx2, was set at the:
questions.e: Tiger range countries pledged at the Global Tiger Summit in Russia to double tigers by the next Year of the Tiger, 2022. India's count reached this target earlier than the deadline.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Project Elephant:
1. It was launched in 1992.
2. The elephant was declared the National Heritage Animal in 2010.
3. It focuses exclusively on captive elephants in temples.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The project aims at protecting wild elephants, their habitats and corridors, and reducing human-elephant conflict. It is not limited to captive animals.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q: The Crocodile Conservation Project, launched in 1975, aimed at protecting which species?
questions.e: The project used captive breeding and rearing for the three crocodilian species native to India. The National Chambal Sanctuary protects the gharial.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q:
Statement-I: Conservationists have proposed establishing a second wild population of Asiatic lions outside Gir.
Statement-II: A single population confined to one landscape is highly vulnerable to epidemics and catastrophes.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Keeping all lions in the Gir region risks a single disease outbreak or natural disaster wiping them out, so a second home is promoted. Statement-II is the reason.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q: A major recent threat to the Great Indian Bustard in its Thar habitat is:
o: collision with overhead high-tension power lines
questions.e: The heavy-bodied bird has poor frontal vision and cannot easily avoid power lines, leading to frequent fatal collisions. Habitat loss to farming and infrastructure adds to the decline.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the snow leopard:
1. Project Snow Leopard was launched in 2009.
2. It is the state animal of Himachal Pradesh.
3. In India it is confined to Arunachal Pradesh alone.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The snow leopard lives across the Himalayan states and Union Territories including Ladakh, Himachal, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal. It is not limited to Arunachal Pradesh.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q: The red panda in India is mainly found in:
o: Sikkim, West Bengal's Singalila region and Arunachal Pradesh
questions.e: The red panda is a bamboo-eating mammal of eastern Himalayan temperate forests with bamboo understorey. It is not found in the southern or desert regions of India.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q: Which one of the following mammals is widely regarded as the most trafficked mammal in the world, for its scales?
questions.e: Pangolin scales are in demand in traditional medicine markets. Indian and Chinese pangolins occur in India and have the highest protection under the Wildlife Act.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Namdapha National Park:
1. It is located in Arunachal Pradesh.
2. The Namdapha flying squirrel is endemic to it.
3. It is home to four big cat species: tiger, leopard, snow leopard and clouded leopard.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Namdapha spans a very wide altitude range in the Eastern Himalaya, from tropical forest to snow peaks, which supports these cats. Its flying squirrel is known only from this area.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q:
The greater one-horned rhinoceros in India is found in:
1. Kaziranga National Park
2. Manas National Park
3. Dudhwa National Park
Select the correct answer.
questions.e: Kaziranga holds the largest population, and rhinos have been reintroduced to Manas and Dudhwa. They are also found in Pobitora and Jaldapara.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Kashmir stag (Hangul):
1. It is a subspecies of the red deer.
2. Its last viable population lives in Dachigam National Park.
3. It is endemic to the Western Ghats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Hangul is restricted to Dachigam in the Kashmir valley and nearby forests, far from the Western Ghats.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment, Indian Flora and Fauna

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980:
1. It requires prior approval of the Central Government for using forest land for non-forest purposes.
2. It was enacted after forests were moved from the State List to the Concurrent List.
3. It applies only to national parks and sanctuaries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment (1976) moved forests to the Concurrent List, allowing Parliament to legislate on them. The Act covers forest land generally, not just national parks and sanctuaries.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions
questions.h: 42nd Amendment gave Parliament the forest key

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 2023:
1. It is the amended and renamed Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980.
2. It exempts certain strategic linear projects within 100 km of international borders or the Line of Control from forest clearance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The 2023 amendment renamed the 1980 Act and eased clearance for specified strategic and security projects near borders, a change that critics said weakens forest protection in sensitive regions.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q: In the T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad case (1996), the Supreme Court:
o: struck down the Indian Forest Act, 1927
applied the Forest Conservation Act to all areas that are forests in the dictionary sense, irrespective of ownership
handed forest management to Gram Sabhas
questions.e: The court gave a broad meaning to 'forest', extending the Act's protection beyond notified forests, and used continuing mandamus to supervise forest matters.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q: Under the Indian Forest Act, 1927, which category of forest has the strictest restrictions on local people's rights?
questions.e: In reserved forests, everything is prohibited unless specifically permitted, while in protected forests the position is reversed. Village forests are assigned to communities.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Forest Rights Act, 2006:
1. The Gram Sabha initiates the process of determining individual and community forest rights.
2. Other Traditional Forest Dwellers must show residence in the forest for at least 75 years to be eligible.
3. The Act applies only to Scheduled Tribes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The FRA covers Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers who have lived in forests for three generations (75 years). The Gram Sabha receives claims and recommends them upward.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q:
With reference to the Forest Rights Act, 2006, consider the following:
1. Title to forest land under occupation up to 4 hectares
2. Ownership of minor forest produce collected by communities
3. Habitat rights for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups
4. Right to hunt wildlife in sanctuaries
How many of the above are recognised by the Act?
questions.e: The Act recognises title, use rights, community rights, habitat rights and the right to protect and conserve community forest resources. It does not confer a right to hunt.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q: The Supreme Court's 2013 judgment on the Niyamgiri hills, regarding a proposed bauxite mine, stressed the role of:
o: the State Pollution Control Board alone
the National Green Tribunal in clearing projects
Gram Sabhas of the Dongria Kondh villages in deciding on religious and community rights
questions.e: The court directed that the Gram Sabhas be consulted under the Forest Rights Act, and they rejected the project. The case is a landmark for tribal rights over forests.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972:
1. The Chief Wildlife Warden can permit hunting of an animal that has become dangerous to human life.
2. The National Board for Wildlife is chaired by the Prime Minister.
3. The Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife is chaired by the Prime Minister.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The NBWL replaced the Indian Board for Wildlife through the 2002 amendment and is chaired by the Prime Minister, but its Standing Committee is chaired by the Environment Minister.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q: The Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 is notable because it:
o: transferred wildlife to the State List
gave effect to CITES provisions and reduced the number of schedules
questions.e: The amendment brought CITES-listed species into the Act, restructured the schedules and added provisions on invasive alien species. It did not move wildlife out of the Concurrent List.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB):
1. It is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
2. It was established by an amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
3. It is headquartered in Dehradun.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The WCCB combats organised wildlife crime and works with enforcement agencies. It is headquartered in New Delhi.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q:
With reference to the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, consider the following:
1. It provides a three-tier structure of the National Biodiversity Authority, State Biodiversity Boards and Biodiversity Management Committees.
2. The National Biodiversity Authority is headquartered in Chennai.
3. State Governments can notify Biodiversity Heritage Sites.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The Act was enacted to implement the CBD, and the NBA was set up in 2003. Section 37 lets State Governments notify areas of biodiversity importance as heritage sites.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions
questions.h: NBA - Nation to Block to Area: NBA, SBB, BMC

questions.q: Which was the first Biodiversity Heritage Site of India, notified in 2007?
questions.e: The grove, with ancient tamarind trees dating to the Chola period, was notified under Section 37 of the Biological Diversity Act. Heritage sites differ from protected areas because they allow use.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q: People's Biodiversity Registers are prepared by:
o: Biodiversity Management Committees at the local body level
questions.e: BMCs in local bodies document local biological resources and associated knowledge, which can support benefit sharing and protect against biopiracy.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 created a three-tier institutional structure from national to local level.
Statement-II: The Act was passed to give effect to India's obligations under the Convention on Biological Diversity.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct. The three-tier structure is a design choice for implementation and is not explained by India's treaty obligation itself, so Statement-II does not directly explain Statement-I.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of institutions and their headquarters:
1. Botanical Survey of India : Kolkata
2. Zoological Survey of India : Kolkata
3. National Biodiversity Authority : Chennai
4. Forest Survey of India : Kolkata
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Forest Survey of India, which publishes the India State of Forest Report, is based in Dehradun. BSI was founded in 1890 and ZSI in 1916.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the India State of Forest Report (ISFR):
1. It is published by the Forest Survey of India every two years.
2. Forest cover includes only legally notified Reserved and Protected forests.
3. Open forest has a canopy density between 10 and 40 percent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Forest cover in the report covers all land over one hectare with tree canopy density above 10 percent regardless of legal status, so statement 2 is wrong.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q: The Wildlife Institute of India (WII) is:
o: a statutory body that regulates zoos
a body of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs
an autonomous institution under the MoEFCC at Dehradun that trains wildlife managers and conducts research
questions.e: WII, set up in 1982, supports Indian wildlife research and works with NTCA on tiger estimation. Zoo regulation belongs to the Central Zoo Authority.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Forest Policy, 1988:
1. It set a goal of bringing one-third of India's geographical area under forest or tree cover.
2. It gave priority to ecological balance over commercial exploitation.
3. It recommended bringing two-thirds of hilly areas under forest cover.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The policy sets 33 percent overall and two-thirds in hills and mountainous regions. Its emphasis on involving local people led to Joint Forest Management.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q: Joint Forest Management in India is generally traced to the experiment at:
questions.e: The Arabari forest officer experiment in the early 1970s shared benefits with communities for protecting the forest. The 1988 forest policy and a 1990 government circular spread the idea.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q: The National Wildlife Action Plan (2017-2031) is the:
o: plan of the National Biodiversity Authority
third such plan, following those of 1983 and 2002-2016
plan that replaced the Wildlife (Protection) Act
questions.e: India's first NWAP was adopted in 1983, and the second covered 2002 to 2016. The current plan emphasises climate change, people's participation and conserving areas outside protected areas.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q: The Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016 deals with:
o: rewards paid to informers on wildlife crime
compensation paid to farmers for crop loss from wildlife
financing of the Tiger Reserve staff salaries only
money paid by user agencies for diversion of forest land, used for afforestation and related activities
questions.e: Agencies that divert forest land for non-forest use pay for compensatory afforestation and the Net Present Value of forest. The Act sets up funds at the national and State levels.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about constitutional provisions on the environment:
1. Article 48A, a Directive Principle, directs the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife.
2. Article 51A(g) makes it a fundamental duty of every citizen to protect and improve the natural environment.
3. Both were inserted by the 44th Constitutional Amendment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Both provisions were inserted by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, not the 44th. The 42nd Amendment also moved forests and protection of wild animals and birds to the Concurrent List.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q:
Statement-I: Parliament could enact the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 to implement decisions of the Stockholm Conference.
Statement-II: Article 253 empowers Parliament to make laws for implementing international agreements and decisions.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 253 lets Parliament legislate on State subjects to implement international commitments, which is the basis for the 1986 Act enacted after the Bhopal gas tragedy.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Animal Welfare Board of India:
1. It is a statutory advisory body established under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960.
2. It was founded in 1962 with Rukmini Devi Arundale as a pioneer.
3. It is a body under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Board works under the 1960 Act and not the Wildlife Act, and advises the Government on animal welfare laws.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions

questions.q: The Indian Board for Wildlife (1952) was replaced by a statutory body through which step?
o: The 2002 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act creating the National Board for Wildlife
questions.e: The Indian Board for Wildlife was a non-statutory advisory body. The National Board for Wildlife became statutory and is chaired by the Prime Minister.
questions.s: Laxmikanth / Shankar IAS Environment, Acts and Institutions
